or on the figure a statement bound, and the floor is applied last: a claim's live due is the

request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The order of the due steps changes: the late charge is now worked out on the rate figure alone,
or on the figure a statement bound, and the floor is applied last: a claim's live due is the
greater of the floor in force on its date and its figure plus its late charge. A statement now
binds the rate figure, not the floored one. Settled figures stay frozen; a correction is unchanged
(no floor, no charge).

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The due steps are now in the new order, and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec.

A claim's live due is now the greater of two things: the floor in force on its date, and its figure plus its late charge. The figure is the rate figure, or the figure a statement bound. The late charge is now worked out on that figure without the floor.

What changed, in the server and the front end alike:

- **`ClaimService`**: the rate figure is no longer floored; the floor is now applied at the end, after the late charge. The same order applies when a steward re-settles a claim. Because a statement stores that figure, it now binds the rate figure rather than the floored one.
- **`RollupService`**: the totals and the audit `ROLLUP`/`TOTALS` lines work the dues out in the same order.
- **`claims.ts`**: the screen's own due calculation (`claimDueCents`) follows the same order, so the screen matches the server.
- Settled dues stay frozen, and corrections still get no floor and no charge. The comments that described the old order are updated.

One thing to know: I didn't migrate any data. A claim already bound by a statement taken before this change keeps the floored figure stored then, because the unfloored figure wasn't saved and can't be recovered from the store. Those claims come right at their person's next statement.
